title: Complex Plane Euler Visualizer
description: A unit vector on the complex plane with color-coded real and imaginary projections and a live substitution of Euler's formula, plus a magnitude readout pinned at 1.00.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Mathematics
Complex Analysis

educational.topic: Euler's formula on the complex plane
learningObjectives: Demonstrate that Re(e^(i theta)) = cos theta and Im(e^(i theta)) = sin theta
Calculate both components for a given angle
Explain why the magnitude is always 1
prerequisites: Sine and cosine as unit-circle coordinates
A complex number has real and imaginary parts

assumptions: Unit magnitude only; scaled complex exponentials are not shown
limitations: Does not cover complex exponentials with a real exponent component (growth or decay)

keyQuestions: Why is the magnitude 1 even when the real part is negative?
What does multiplying by e^(i theta) do to a complex number?
commonMisconceptions: That a negative real part implies a negative magnitude
That Euler's formula is a definition rather than something checkable
assessmentOpportunities: State the components and magnitude of e^(i pi)
